newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania leaders pledge to recognise vote.
newsitem.headline: Albania leaders pledge to recognise vote.

text.p: Albanian leaders cast their ballots on Sunday in a crucial general election, pledging they would respect the outcome of the poll but hinting they were not prepared to work with their rivals should the result be close.

President Sali Berisha of the right-leaning Democratic Party cast his vote with his wife Liri in a school classroom crammed with television crews and reporters near his modest apartment in central Tirana.
"I am definitely going to accept the results," Berisha said in English in response to a reporter's question. "I will fully recognise the elections."
Asked if he would step down if his party lost, Berisha said it was too early to consider the concept of 'cohabitation' in Albania, suggesting he would be unable to work with a leftist government.
Socialist leader Fatos Nano voted in a school in central Tirana, telling reporters the poll marked the first step on Albania's road towards Western integration.
"These elections are of extraordinary importance. This will be a society of free citizens which will not be different from other European nations," he said. "Tomorrow will be a new day."
Nano also hinted that his party would not be prepared to go into a coalition with the Democrats.
"Albania has its own pecularities. Do not look for classical formulas of cohabitation here," he said.
Sunday's early poll was called after a wave of violence, triggered by the collapse of investment schemes, swept the troubled Balkan nation.
